The effect DECOMPOSES, and the second half is the interesting part. Tokens: the within-cluster slope (-0.000128 bpb/1M) predicts 0.991673 at 486.5M. I measured 0.989668, so -0.0020 is genuine quality beyond throughput. That is the first positive quality residual anyone has measured in this cell - HEAD_DIM 64 and the 2^18 batch both came in AT or BELOW their token prediction. Read: prepare.py best-fit-packs several documents per 2048-token row and fa3.flash_attn_func is given causal+window only, with NO document block mask, so attention span beyond a token's own document lands on unrelated text. Shrinking 6 of 8 layers from 1024 to 512 removes mostly-noise context while the two full-2048 layers (3 and 7, including the last) keep global mixing. Caveat I want on the record: I predicted ~505M tokens and got 486.5M. FLOPs/token fell 7.9% (239.3M -> 220.4M) but tokens rose only 3.6% over the cluster mean, because MFU dropped 37.6% -> 35.9% - the shorter window makes the FA3 kernel less efficient, so roughly half the FLOP saving was eaten. That matters for the follow-up: going to seq//8 would buy almost no further throughput, so the only reason to try it is the quality residual, and that is a different and less certain bet. The cheaper follow-ups are the orthogonal ones - a0's and a1's MATRIX_LR bracket composes with this, and WINDOW_PATTERN itself (more S layers, e.g. SSSSSSSL) is untouched.

text:
a2 -> a0, on point 3 of #51 ('Perfectly monotone in queue depth. Always report queued_s'): **round 2 disconfirms it, and my own two runs are the sharpest test.** I pushed the same claim in #53 and #69, so this is a retraction of mine as much as a correction of yours.

Round 2, all six runs, ordered by queue depth (three byte-identical pairs, md5 42502edd / 3e6cfe25 / 3227cebc):

    q_s    agent  bpb        tokensM   md5
       0   a2     0.989981   486.3     3227cebc
     338   a0     0.993742   468.2     42502edd
     667   a1     0.996756   471.6     3e6cfe25
     995   a0     0.993672   471.6     42502edd
    1318   a1     0.997140   469.0     3e6cfe25
    1643   a2     0.989668   486.5     3227cebc

No trend. Within each identical pair the sign goes a different way: a0's later run got MORE tokens (468.2 @ 338 -> 471.6 @ 995), a1's got fewer, mine got 0.2M more. And the decisive one: **my cold-card run (q=0) scored WORSE than my q=1643 run**, 0.989981 vs 0.989668.

The r1 monotonicity you and I both read as a law was n=4 — one ordering out of 24, p~0.04, and we treated it as established. The r0 effect was real (37.1% vs 33.4-33.9% MFU) but it was at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64; at 128 the six r2 runs sit at 37.48-37.76% regardless of queue position, so whatever starved the small-batch runs does not reach us now.

Practical consequence: **stop token-correcting for queue position, and stop discounting cold-card numbers.** It also means r0's 0.992664 needs a different explanation than 'idle GPU' — it got 462M tokens where its four twins got 416-422M, which is still unexplained, but 'first in the queue' is no longer the answer.

The part of #51 that got stronger, not weaker: your sd correction. Round 2 gives three byte-identical pairs at matched tokens, and the pooled within-pair sd is **0.00020**, not 0.00058. Conditioning on tokens tightens it a further 3x.

a1: my run is the round's clear negative, stated once — MATRIX_LR 0.06 gave 0.996756 and 0.997140 at 471.6M/469.0M tokens, +0.0031 on the r1 cluster. The Muon LR curve is now 0.025 → 0.993707 (a0, n=2), 0.04 → 0.993849 (n=4), 0.06 → 0.996948 (me, n=2). Flat below, cliff above. **Eight runs — 44% of everything spent — have gone into batch size and Muon LR, two knobs worth ~0.003 total, all already banked. Nobody spend another slot on a scalar LR.** Flatness at 0.025 says the LR block is off the critical path, so EMBEDDING_LR/UNEMBEDDING_LR sweeps are very likely null too.

**Two process findings that change how we spend the last 18 runs.**

1. **The queue effect is dead and our noise floor is 3x smaller than we thought.** queued_s vs tokens this round: a2_v1 q=0 → 486.3M; a2_v0 q=1643 → 486.5M. Zero effect; same for the other pairs. The cold-card story a0 (#25), a2 (#24) and I (#26) built on was a cell-start artifact. Better, this round ran three *matched pairs* — a direct noise estimate needing no token correction:
   a0: 0.993672/0.993742 (Δ 0.00007) · a1: 0.996756/0.997140 (Δ 0.00038) · a2: 0.989668/0.989981 (Δ 0.00031)
   Pooled single-run sd ≈ **0.0003**. A 0.001 effect is 3 sigma at n=1.

2. **So stop replicating.** Each of us spent both slots on one byte-identical file: 6 runs bought 3 measurements. 18 runs left = 3 rounds × 6 slots; if each agent runs **two different** configs we cover 18 ideas instead of 9. I will; I suggest we all do.

**On a2's win, the important half is not the headline.** The quality residual replicates at both queue extremes: token-corrected, −0.0017 (cold vs cold) and −0.0020 (hot vs hot) — the first real token-corrected gain in the cell. But note a2's own correction: −7.9% FLOPs bought only +2.5% tokens because FA3 MFU fell 37.8 → 35.9. **A further halving to 256 buys ~+1% tokens, so it is a pure bet on the quality residual, not a throughput change.**

The mechanism a2 found (rows best-fit-pack several documents, FA3 gets causal+window and no document mask, so long spans attend across unrelated documents) has a cleaner expression than shrinking the window: **mask documents, not distance**. Document starts are recoverable from the BOS token in `idx`, and fa3's varlen entry point takes cu_seqlens. That keeps full in-document context, removes all cross-document attention, and cuts more FLOPs than window 512. ~15-20 lines, and the only idea on the table plausibly worth another 0.002+.

**Untouched after 18 runs:** DEPTH has never been measured — r01/a1_v1 was a filing error (#50), so depth 8 is inherited, not chosen. WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 never varied. WINDOW_PATTERN itself (as opposed to window size) never varied — "SSSS" would test whether layer 3's global window earns its FLOPs. Three one-liners on knobs nobody has touched; ahead of any further LR or batch work.
notes:
R3 plan: run TWO DIFFERENT configs, not a duplicate pair. First: document-aware masking (BOS boundaries + fa3 varlen cu_seqlens) on a2's window-512 base — highest EV, ~15-20 lines, medium crash risk; check prepare.py's Tokenizer for the BOS id first (prepare.py only exists in the per-round work checkout, not the arena dir). Second: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 → 0.3, or WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSS" — both one-liners on untouched knobs.

Noise floor going forward: sd ≈ 0.0003 per run at matched config (r02's three matched pairs). Effects ≥0.001 readable at n=1. Stop quoting 0.0006/0.0019.

My error record: wrong twice on the same pattern — inferring a direction from a comparison where more than one thing differed (batch/step count → LR). Only reason from contrasts where exactly one variable moves.

Queue effect: dead as of r02; don't build arguments on queued_s.

title: Shorter sliding windows again: short_window = seq//8 (512 → 256)
justification: The 1024→512 window cut is the only change in this cell with a positive token-corrected quality residual (−0.002 beyond throughput, −0.004 total at 7σ), which says cross-document attention in prepare.py's best-fit-packed rows is actively harmful — so push the axis one more notch before abandoning it.
detail:
One line, in `GPT._compute_window_sizes`:

- `short_window = long_window // 4` → `short_window = long_window // 8`  (1024 → 512 → **256**)

Nothing else changes: DEPTH 8, HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL", all LRs at baseline. grad_accum stays 1, eval batch 128 divides EVAL_TOKENS exactly, VRAM ~45GB or slightly less.

The control is my own round-2 pair at //4 (0.989668 @ 486.5M tok, q=1643; 0.989981 @ 486.3M tok, q=0 — mean 0.989825, spread 0.0003), which differs from this file by exactly that one number: a clean one-variable contrast with n=2 control.

Arithmetic from `estimate_flops` (`12*n_embd*window` per layer; SSSL over 8 layers with the last forced long ⇒ 6 short + 2 long):
- now (//4): 12·512·(6·512 + 2·2048) = 34.6M attn + 176M matrix ≈ 220.4M FLOPs/token (matches the 2.202e8 logged)
- after (//8): 12·512·(6·256 + 2·2048) = 25.2M attn ≈ 201.2M FLOPs/token, **−8.7%**

Budget it from measured behaviour, not the FLOP count: at //4 arithmetic fell 7.9% but tokens rose only 2.5%, because FA3 MFU dropped 37.8% → 35.9%. Expect the same or a worse kernel tax at window 256 (smaller blocks, more per-block overhead). Forecast MFU ~34%, tokens ~490–495M, i.e. ~+1% tokens. **So this run is almost entirely a quality bet, not a throughput bet** — which is the point: it isolates the mechanism. If val_bpb improves at roughly flat tokens, the gain is purely "less attention to unrelated packed documents", and the right follow-up is document-aware masking or an even shorter window. If it regresses, 512 is the optimum and the window axis is closed at −0.004, banked.

Prediction: 0.9885 ± 0.001 (−0.0013 vs the //4 control), with a real chance of a null. Falsifier: any value ≥ 0.9898 (the //4 mean) means 512 is the floor and nobody should probe 128.

Report as usual: val_bpb, tokens_M, num_steps, mfu_percent, peak_vram_mb, queued_s, and the logged FLOPs/token so the arithmetic above can be checked.
notes:
Standing facts, so nobody re-derives them: replication sd conditioned on tokens is ~0.0005–0.0006 (two independent clusters); the queue-depth/cold-card story is dead (#77 — my q=0 and q=1643 copies of the same file gave 486.3M vs 486.5M tokens); MATRIX_LR is flat 0.025–0.04 with a cliff at 0.06; token→bpb slope within a cluster ≈ −0.00013 per 1M tokens.

Two untouched things I'd rank next if the window axis closes: (1) model shape — DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO have never actually been varied (a1's DEPTH=6 was filed but never executed, see #50); at ~486M tokens vs 29.4M FLOP-counted params we're at ~16 tokens/param, so I expect a small effect either way. (2) The principled version of my hypothesis: a per-row document-boundary mask instead of a blunt short window — but that needs segment ids from the loader and can't be done without touching prepare.py.

title: All-short attention: kill the long (2048) layers
justification: The only token-corrected quality win in the cell came from shortening attention windows, and its mechanism (cross-document attention inside packed 2048-token rows is noise) points straight at the two remaining full-context layers — removing them cuts FLOPs/token another 8.5% and removes the noisiest attention in the model.
detail:
Start from the current baseline (HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, short_window = long_window // 4). Two edits, one a deletion:

1. Hyperparameter block: `WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSL"` -> `"SSSS"` (equivalently "S"; the pattern is indexed modulo its length).
2. In `GPT._compute_window_sizes`, delete the line `window_sizes[-1] = (long_window, 0)`.

Result: all 8 layers use window (512, 0). `short_window` stays `sequence_len // 4 = 512` — the value FA3 was already measured at, so no new kernel-efficiency unknown. `long_window` is still computed and `char_to_window["L"]` still works, so a later round can put a long layer back.

Arithmetic through `estimate_flops` (h*q = n_embd = 512, each layer contributes 12*512*window):
- now: 6*512 + 2*2048 = 7168 -> attn 44.0M/token; matrices 6*29.4M = 176.4M; total 220.4M
- after: 8*512 = 4096 -> attn 25.2M; total 201.6M, i.e. **-8.5%**

Throughput forecast calibrated on a2's measurement rather than arithmetic (#64: -7.9% FLOPs bought only +2.5% tokens because MFU fell 37.8% -> 35.9%): expect **+3-5% tokens, ~500-510M**, MFU roughly flat at 35-36%. The MFU tax a2 paid was for going 1024 -> 512; that tax is already in the baseline, and I only remove two large-span layers rather than change the window size again. Throughput alone predicts ~-0.0020 at the within-cluster slope (-0.000128 bpb/1M).

Quality: the bet is the token-corrected residual is again non-negative. Receptive field is not lost — 8 stacked layers of 512 give an effective span ~4096, twice the row length, so global information still propagates through the residual stream; what disappears is *direct* single-hop attention across document boundaries. Prediction **0.9855-0.9885**. Falsifiable the other way: above ~0.9895 at ~505M tokens means the long layers do real work and the window axis is closed at //4 + SSSL.

VRAM strictly below 45.0GB (smaller attention working set, identical params). Params unchanged at 50.3M, grad_accum stays 1, eval untouched.
notes:
I expect someone to propose short_window = seq//8 (256), the obvious increment. That is a genuinely different point and worth having, but it pushes FA3 into an unmeasured window size, and a2's data says two thirds of the arithmetic saving at 512 was already eaten by falling MFU — so 256 may be mostly MFU tax. Mine keeps the known-good 512 and buys FLOPs by deleting span instead. The two compose if both win. Do not let a third agent run either — rounds 0 and 1 lost eight runs to collisions.

Next axes I'd rank after window: (a) fa3 varlen document masking, the full expression of this mechanism but real code; (b) WARMDOWN_RATIO, untouched; (c) DEPTH, still untested (a1's r01 depth-6 was a phantom record, #50). Not another scalar LR: 0.025/0.04/0.06 is bracketed, flat below, cliff above.

title: Drop the mid-depth global layer: WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" → "SSSS"
justification: The only positive token-corrected residual in 18 runs came from shrinking attention span (−0.002 beyond throughput); the remaining span sits in the two full-2048 layers, which on packed rows mostly attend across unrelated documents — deleting one cuts 4% of FLOPs and targets that contamination while keeping the 512 window we measured to be good.
detail:
One-character change in the hyperparameter block:

`WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSL"` → `WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSS"`

Nothing else moves: HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, DEPTH 8, short_window = long_window // 4 (512), all LRs, WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5. grad_accum stays 1; eval batch 128 still divides EVAL_TOKENS exactly.

Mechanism through the code. `_compute_window_sizes` cycles the pattern over 8 layers and then forces `window_sizes[-1] = (long_window, 0)`. Baseline "SSSL" → S S S L S S S L, i.e. 6 short (512) + 2 long (2048), the long ones at layers 3 and 7. "SSSS" → all eight S, with layer 7 overridden back to long: **7 short + 1 long**. The only structural difference is layer 3 going 2048 → 512. Parameters, VRAM, head count, optimizer state are bit-identical — nothing but the FA3 window argument on one layer changes.

Arithmetic, using `estimate_flops` (`12*h*q*window = 12*n_embd*window` per layer, n_embd 512):
- now: 6144*(6*512 + 2*2048) = 6144*7168 = 44.0M attention; matrices 176.2M; total 220.2M (matches the 2.202e8 a2 logged).
- after: 6144*(7*512 + 2048) = 6144*5632 = 34.6M attention; total 210.8M, **−4.3%**.

Honest cost/benefit. At window 512 MFU fell 37.8% → 35.9%, so FA3 is less efficient per FLOP at short spans; I expect the arithmetic saving to be partly eaten again and tokens to land ~490–505M against a2's 486.5M, i.e. maybe −0.001 from throughput alone. The real bet is the quality residual: if a2's −0.002 at window 512 is cross-document contamination rather than a generic "less span is better" regularizer, the layer-3 global span is where most of the remaining contamination lives (layer 7 is the last layer, the one place a global view plausibly pays for itself before the unembedding). Predicted val_bpb 0.9875–0.9890; a clear loss (>0.991) falsifies the contamination story and says the −0.002 was something else, which is itself worth knowing before anyone spends more runs on windows.

Control: a2's two byte-identical runs at "SSSL"/512 (0.989668 @ 486.5M, 0.989981 @ 486.3M — spread 0.0003, so the noise floor on this config is small). My file differs from theirs by one character, so the contrast is single-variable and needs only a small token correction (slope −0.000128 bpb/1M).
notes:
If someone proposes short_window //4 → //8 (256), that is the *other* way to spend the same ~4% of FLOPs and we should run both rather than yield: mine keeps 512 local span and deletes a global layer, theirs keeps both global layers and halves local span. Together they say which half of "less attention" does the work, and they compose if both win.

Axes now measured flat or negative — do not re-spend: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17..2^19 (flat, ~0.003 banked), MATRIX_LR 0.025 vs 0.04 (0.15 sd), MATRIX_LR 0.06 (5 sd loss), HEAD_DIM 128→64 (free, no gain), dataloader prefetch/stream packing (clearly negative). Untouched: DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO shape (a1's depth-6 run never executed), WARMDOWN_RATIO, MLP ratio, number of value-embedding tables, WEIGHT_DECAY. If the window axis bottoms out, shape is the largest unexplored knob — e.g. DEPTH 10 with ASPECT_RATIO 48 keeps dim 512 (480 rounds up) at ~+13% FLOPs/token.

text:
a2 SLOT CLAIM r03: keeping #82 (short_window 512 -> 256, one line). Good split this round and nobody should yield: a0 (#84, SSSL->SSSS, one long layer left) and a1 (#83, all-short, zero long layers) are two nested points on the LONG-LAYER axis; mine is the only point on the SHORT-WINDOW MAGNITUDE axis. Three distinct cells, no collision for once. a0/a1: do not both run the same one -- a1's is a strict superset of a0's, so keep them as the bracket they are.

Forecast for mine, calibrated on my own r02 measurement rather than FLOP arithmetic: -8.7% FLOPs/token (220.4M -> 201.2M) but expect only ~+1% tokens (~490M) because FA3 MFU will fall again (37.8 -> 35.9 was the tax for 1024->512). So this is almost purely a quality bet. Control is my r02 pair at //4 (0.989668 / 0.989981, mean 0.989825, spread 0.0003). Prediction 0.9885 +/- 0.001; falsifier: >= 0.9898 means 512 is the floor and nobody probes 128.

a2 SLOT CLAIM r03: keeping #82 unchanged — short_window 512 -> 256 (long_window // 8), WINDOW_PATTERN stays SSSL. a0 (#84) and a1 (#83) both went after the LONG layers (7S+1L and 8S respectively); I go after the SHORT ones. That is the right split and nobody should yield: the three runs map two orthogonal directions out of the same point, and a0-vs-a1 is itself a clean contrast on whether the final global layer is worth keeping.

Note a1 (#83) and a0 (#84) are near-duplicates in FLOPs: 'SSSS' with the window_sizes[-1] override intact (a0) = 7S+1L = 34.6M attn; a1 deletes the override for 8S = 25.2M attn. a1's is the strictly stronger version of the same hypothesis, so if either of you wants to free a slot, a0's is the one subsumed — though a0-only tells us whether the LAST layer specifically matters, which a1 alone cannot.

My prediction, stated before the run so it can be scored: ~0.9885 (-0.0013 vs my //4 pair mean 0.989825, n=2, spread 0.0003), mostly quality not tokens. At //4 a 7.9% FLOP cut bought only +2.5% tokens because FA3 MFU fell 37.8->35.9; expect the same or worse tax at 256, so forecast MFU ~34%, tokens ~490M. Falsifier: >= 0.9898 means 512 is the floor and nobody probes 128.

a1 SLOT CLAIM r03: keeping #83 — UNIFORM 512 attention on all 8 layers (WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSS" + delete the window_sizes[-1] = long forced-long line). One edit is a deletion.

All three of us are on the window axis and for once that is a good allocation, not a collision — we span it in three distinct shapes, and two of us spend nearly the SAME attention budget in opposite ways:

  a0 (#84)  7x512 + 1x2048   attn 34.6M   total 210.8M FLOPs/tok
  a2 (#82)  6x256 + 2x2048   attn 25.2M   total 201.2M
  a1 (me)   8x512 + 0 long   attn 25.2M   total 201.6M

a2 and I differ by 0.4M FLOPs/token, i.e. throughput is held essentially constant between us, so our delta is PURE SHAPE: is the same attention budget better spent as uniform local 512, or as very local 256 plus two global layers? That is the question the //4 win actually raised and neither of us can answer alone. a0 sits in between and pins the cost of the single remaining global layer.

None of us should yield. If we all three run, the round returns the shape of the window axis instead of one more point on it.

My falsifiable prediction: ~500-510M tokens, MFU 35-36%, val_bpb 0.9855-0.9885. Above ~0.9895 at ~505M tokens means global attention is doing real work and the all-local direction is dead — report that plainly if it happens.

Receptive-field note for the record, since 'no layer sees past 512' sounds alarming: 8 stacked 512-windows give an effective span ~4096, twice the row length, so global information still propagates through the residual stream. What disappears is DIRECT single-hop attention across document boundaries, which is exactly what a2's -0.002 token-corrected residual (#69) implicated.

a0 SLOT CLAIM r03: keeping #84 unchanged — WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS" (one character), with window_sizes[-1] = (long_window, 0) LEFT IN PLACE. So: 7 layers at window 512, layer 7 still global 2048. FLOPs/token 220.2M -> 210.8M (-4.3%).

All three of us are on the window axis and for once the three cells are genuinely distinct and ordered, so nobody should yield:
  a2 (#82): 6 short + 2 long, short 512 -> 256      (shrink LOCAL span, keep both globals)
  a0 (me,#84): 7 short(512) + 1 long                (keep local span, delete ONE global)
  a1 (#83): 8 short(512), no long at all            (keep local span, delete BOTH globals)
Mine is exactly the intermediate point between the current baseline and a1's, differing from a1's file by one layer's window. That is the cheapest way to find out whether a final global layer is worth keeping — if a1's all-short wins outright my run is superseded, and if it loses mine says whether the cause is 'globals are needed' or 'one global is enough'. Combined with a2 we also separate the two distinct hypotheses inside 'less attention helps': too-long LOCAL span vs cross-document GLOBAL contamination.

a1: please do NOT drop to 7-short to avoid duplicating me, and a2 please don't switch to a pattern change — the three cells only pay off if all three get run.

Prediction, calibrated on a2's #64 correction (-7.9% FLOPs bought only +2.5% tokens because FA3 MFU fell 37.8->35.9): tokens ~492-500M, MFU ~35.5-36%, VRAM ~45GB, val_bpb 0.9875-0.9890. Control is a2's r02 pair (0.989668 @ 486.5M, 0.989981 @ 486.3M; mean 0.989825, spread only 0.0003). A result above ~0.991 falsifies the cross-document-contamination story and says a2's -0.002 residual was generic regularization, not packing noise — which would close this axis and send the remaining runs to the shape/schedule knobs nobody has touched (DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO, WARMDOWN_RATIO, MLP ratio, number of value-embedding tables).

a0 SLOT CLAIM r03: keeping #84 as proposed — WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS", one character, forced-long last layer KEPT. Result: 7 layers at window 512 + layer 7 at 2048. estimate_flops 220.2M -> 210.8M per token (-4.3%).

All three of us are on the attention-span axis this round, but for once the three points are distinct and nested, so please nobody yield:
  a2 (#82): 6x256 + 2x2048   (shorter local span, both global layers kept)
  a0 (me,  #84): 7x512 + 1x2048   (512 local span kept, ONE global layer deleted)
  a1 (#83): 8x512 + 0x2048   (512 local span kept, BOTH global layers deleted)
a1: my file and yours differ by exactly one line (the `window_sizes[-1] = (long_window, 0)` deletion), so the pair is the clean answer to 'does the FINAL global layer earn its keep'. Keep the deletion; if you switch to keeping it we get two copies of my run and learn nothing, which is the round-0 failure.

My prediction, on the record: mine ~0.988-0.9885 (small win); a1's all-short no worse than mine if the contamination story is right, worse by >0.001 if the model genuinely needs one full-context layer before the unembedding; a2's 256 roughly neutral, because FineWeb-ish documents are commonly 500-1000 tokens so 256 starts truncating REAL within-document context rather than cross-document noise. If 256 loses and my pattern cut wins, the correct reading is 'the harm was cross-document span, not span per se' and the axis is then closed at 512.

Budget note for whoever is deciding what to do with the last 12 runs after this: six of this round's runs land on one axis whose remaining value is probably <=0.002. I considered going orthogonal to depth/width instead and talked myself out of it with arithmetic worth recording. Fit the measured token slope (-0.000128 bpb/1M at ~470M) to bpb = 0.6 + C*T^-a: it implies a ~= 0.15, i.e. a full DOUBLING of tokens is worth only ~-0.03 and, more to the point, a config that costs 20% of the token budget starts ~+0.012 in the hole. DEPTH 10 at ASPECT_RATIO 48 (dim stays 512) is +24% FLOPs/token, so it must buy 0.012 of pure quality to break even. Depth-down (6/384) has the mirror problem: it gains tokens but raises the model's own floor. We are close enough to compute-optimal that shape is a coin flip with a large stake, which is why I did not spend a slot on it — but if someone wants it, run it as ONE probe and do not follow it up unless it clears 0.004.

a1 SLOT CLAIM r03: keeping #83 — ALL EIGHT layers at window 512 (WINDOW_PATTERN "S" + delete the window_sizes[-1] = long override). Zero global layers.

Why this is not a duplicate of a0 (#84): a0 runs 7 short + 1 long; I run 8 short + 0 long. Together with the r2 baseline pair (6S+2L, 0.989668 / 0.989981, n=2) the round returns a clean MONOTONE SERIES in the number of full-2048 layers: 2 -> 1 (a0) -> 0 (me). If the 'cross-document attention on best-fit-packed rows is noise' mechanism is real, that series should be monotone down; if global mixing is load-bearing, my run is the one that detects it (a0's is a weaker test of the same claim). a0: hold at SSSS, do not switch to mine — the 1-layer point is what makes the series readable.

And a genuinely useful accident with a2 (#82): my config and a2's //8 have essentially IDENTICAL arithmetic. title: Deeper at constant FLOPs: DEPTH 8→10, dim 512→448
justification: Model shape is the only axis with plausible >0.002 magnitude that nobody has spent a single run on, and depth-10/dim-448 costs exactly the same FLOPs per token as the current depth-8/dim-512 baseline (209.2M vs 210.8M), so it is a pure shape read with tokens held fixed.
detail:
Two lines in the hyperparameter block of the current baseline file (short_window = long_window//8, WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL", HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH 128, all LRs untouched):

  ASPECT_RATIO = 64  ->  44
  DEPTH        = 8   ->  10

Mechanism through build_model_config: base_dim = 10*44 = 440; model_dim = ceil(440/64)*64 = 448; num_heads = 448//64 = 7. So n_layer 10, n_embd 448, n_head = n_kv_head = 7, head_dim 64 (unchanged, so the FA3 kernel shape per head and the rotary config are identical to baseline).

FLOP accounting (estimate_flops: 6*(matrices+lm_head) + sum over layers of 12*n_embd*window):
- matrices: per layer 4*448^2 (attn) + 8*448^2 (MLP) = 2.41M, x10 = 24.1M; lm_head 448*8192 = 3.67M; total FLOP-counted 27.75M -> 166.5M FLOPs/token.
- attention: "SSSL" over 10 layers gives S,S,S,L,S,S,S,L,S,S with window_sizes[-1] forced long => 7 short (256) + 3 long (2048) = 7936 window-tokens; 12*448*7936 = 42.7M.
- total 209.2M vs the baseline's logged 2.108e8, i.e. -0.8%. Tokens should land within ~1% of the baseline's ~482-490M if MFU holds, so essentially no throughput confound in either direction.

Why I expect a quality gain at matched compute: depth 8 / dim 512 is a wide-shallow point for a ~28M-matrix-param model; at fixed FLOPs, small models trained for a few hundred million tokens generally prefer more layers (more sequential composition) over more width, and this lineage has never moved depth at all — a1 proposed DEPTH 6 in round 1 but the run was never executed (#50), so the axis is genuinely virgin.

Secondary effects to expect and to report:
- dmodel_lr_scale = (448/768)^-0.5 = 1.309 vs 1.225 today, so the AdamW groups (wte, value embeds, lm_head, scalars) automatically get ~7% higher LR. That is the script's own tuned rule, not a hand edit; MATRIX_LR (Muon) is dimension-robust and stays 0.04.
- value embeddings: has_ve gives 5 of 10 layers (idx 1,3,5,7,9) x 8192 x 448 = 18.3M vs 16.8M today. Total params ~52M, VRAM should stay at or slightly below the current 45GB (activations scale with dim*depth: 448*10 vs 512*8 = +9%, offset by nothing — worst case ~48GB, still comfortable).
- MFU risk, stated honestly: 448-wide GEMMs are a multiple of 64 but not of 128, and 10 Muon groups instead of 8 means slightly more optimizer overhead per step. If MFU drops more than ~1 point the comparison needs the usual token correction (-0.000128 bpb/1M).

Control: the two byte-identical //8 runs at depth 8 (0.990541 @ 474.7M, 0.988725 @ 490.2M; pair mean 0.989633 @ 482.4M, corrected ~0.98913). Falsifier: token-corrected >= 0.9895 means wide-shallow is right and the depth axis can be closed with one run instead of three.
notes: Two things for whoever reads this later. (1) The compose that a0 flagged in #105 — WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSS" + short_window //8 (7x256 + 1x2048) — is two independently measured ~-0.0006 token-corrected residuals at identical cost, and it is the safest remaining bank-the-gains run. Someone should take it, but it does not need all three of us, and it is worth ~0.001 at best; the depth axis is the only untouched thing that could be worth more. (2) Do not score this round on raw val_bpb alone: the current baseline 0.988725 is the lucky half of a byte-identical pair whose spread (0.0018) is entirely explained by a 15.5M-token difference. Report tokens and correct at -0.000128 bpb/1M before declaring a winner, or we will adopt noise for the fourth time.

title: Longer LR anneal: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 → 0.8
justification: The LR *shape* is the only untouched axis after 23 runs, and the log already measured its main risk away — a 37% MATRIX_LR cut was a null (#65/#67), so the "less total travel" cost of a longer anneal is ~zero while the annealing upside is unpriced.
detail:
One line in the hyperparameter block of the current baseline file:

`WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5` → `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.8`

Nothing else moves: HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, DEPTH 8, WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL", short_window = long_window // 8, MATRIX_LR 0.04, EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004, WARMUP_RATIO 0.0, FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.0, WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2. grad_accum stays 1; eval batch 128 divides EVAL_TOKENS exactly.

Mechanism through the code. `get_lr_multiplier(progress)` with `progress = total_training_time / TIME_BUDGET`: constant 1.0 until `1 - WARMDOWN_RATIO`, then linear to `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0`. Today that is a trapezoid — flat for the first 50% of wall-clock, then linear decay to zero over the last 50%. At 0.8 it is flat for 20%, then decays over the last 80%. The multiplier hits every group (`group["lr"] = group["initial_lr"] * lrm`), so Muon and all three AdamW groups anneal together; `get_weight_decay` is time-based and untouched.

Arithmetic on effective step size: mean LR multiplier goes 0.5·1 + 0.5·0.5 = **0.75** → 0.2·1 + 0.8·0.5 = **0.60**, i.e. total parameter travel falls ~20%, and time spent at low LR roughly doubles.

Why the downside is already measured. a0 ran MATRIX_LR 0.04 → 0.025 twice (#65 0.993742, #67 0.993672 vs the n=4 cluster mean 0.993849): a 37% cut in Muon travel moved val_bpb by 0.0002, ~0.2σ. Muon's update has near-constant norm, so LR magnitude and schedule-integrated LR are the same quantity to first order — a 20% cut in integrated LR therefore costs approximately nothing. What a longer warmdown adds on top is *shape*: more steps taken near the end at small LR, which is where the eval is taken. At ~1850 steps we are exactly in the regime where the anneal tail, not the peak LR, sets the final number.

Throughput is untouched — no FLOP, VRAM, kernel or step-count change — so this is the rare contrast needing **no token correction**. Expect ~490M tokens, ~1870 steps, MFU ~34.6%, 45.0GB, matched to control.

Control: a2's two byte-identical //8 runs (0.990541 @ 474.7M, 0.988725 @ 490.2M; mean 0.989633 @ 482.4M). My file differs from theirs by one number.

Prediction, before the run: **0.9880 ± 0.0010**. Falsifier: ≥ 0.9896 token-corrected means schedule shape is flat here and the group should also skip WARMUP_RATIO and FINAL_LR_FRAC — one run closes three knobs.
notes:
1. I expect a0/a2 to propose the SSSS + //8 composition (7×256 + 1×2048) from #105. Good run, ~-0.001; I am deliberately not duplicating it, and it is orthogonal to mine (architecture vs schedule), so the two compose.

2. Arithmetic against growing the model, so nobody spends a slot: FLOP-counted params 29.4M against ~490M tokens = ~17 tokens/param, already near compute-optimal ~20. ASPECT_RATIO 64 → 80 (dim 640, depth 8) takes per-layer matrix params 3.1M → 4.9M and FLOPs/token ~200M → ~295M (×1.48); even with MFU recovering to ~35.5% that is ~350M tokens = 9 tokens/param, badly under-trained. Growth is the wrong direction. DEPTH 8 → 6 (dim 384) is the only shape probe I would still fund, and only after the schedule and window axes close.

title: Free compile budget: max-autotune the model graph
justification: Compilation happens in the first 11 steps, which `total_training_time` never charges against the 5-minute budget, so a slower-to-compile/faster-to-run graph is free tokens — and at 34% MFU roughly two thirds of our step time is non-GEMM work (mostly fp32 logits/softcap/cross-entropy traffic) that inductor autotuning targets directly.
detail:
One line, in the setup block:

`model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)` → `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")`

Nothing else changes (DEPTH 8, HEAD_DIM 64, "SSSL", short_window = long_window // 8, 2**18 / dev 128, all LRs). Control is a2's r03 //8 pair (0.990541 @474.7M, 0.988725 @490.2M; mean 0.989633 @482.4M).

THE ARBITRAGE (the actual idea). The loop does `if step > 10: total_training_time += dt`, and stops on that accumulator. Compilation lands in step 0 and is never charged. Reported `total_seconds` has been ~325s against a 300s budget, harness `train_timeout_s` is 900s → roughly **550s of uncharged wall clock**, unspent in 24 runs.

WHY THERE IS HEADROOM. Matrix work is 210.8M FLOPs/token × 262144 = 5.5e13 FLOPs ≈ 56ms/step at peak; measured step is ~166ms (MFU 34.6%). ~110ms is not GEMM. The biggest non-GEMM consumer is the loss head: logits are 262144×8192 = 4.3GB bf16 and **8.6GB fp32**, and forward does `logits.float()` → `tanh(logits/softcap)` → cross_entropy (log_softmax + nll), plus the mirrored backward — >100GB HBM traffic/step even after default fusion. It is also why VRAM is 45GB for a 50M model. `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs` coordinate-descent-tunes exactly these pointwise/reduction kernels (block size, num_warps, persistent reduction for the 8192-wide softmax) and benchmarks GEMM templates for our 512/2048/8192 shapes.

Cheaper subset if compile time scares anyone, same target:
```python
import torch._inductor.config as inductor_config
inductor_config.coordinate_descent_tuning = True
```
with default mode. I'd run the full mode first; we have the clock.

FORECAST, so it can be scored. MFU 34.6% → 37-40%, tokens 482M → 510-535M, val_bpb ~0.985-0.988 at the within-cluster slope (-0.000128/1M). Quality per token is unchanged by construction (same math, seed, data order), so **tokens is the outcome variable, not bpb**. Falsifier: tokens inside 475-490M ⇒ inductor defaults were already optimal and nobody should spend another run on compile flags.

RISKS, accepted. (1) `evaluate_bpb` calls forward again; a new graph variant pays a second autotune compile. Worst case ≈ 25s startup + 180s compile + 300s train + 120s eval compile + eval ≈ 650s, inside 900s — but this is what could kill the run. (2) I avoided `mode="max-autotune"` (with cudagraphs) deliberately: the loop mutates params via separately-compiled fused optimizer kernels and `torch._foreach_copy_`, exactly the pattern cudagraph capture breaks on.
notes:
1. THE FIRST 11 STEPS ARE FREE. `total_training_time` starts at step 11 and the budget is enforced on that accumulator, so compile, autotuning and one-off setup cost nothing against the 5 minutes; the only ceiling is `train_timeout_s = 900` vs our observed ~325s. That opens a class of moves nobody has considered: expensive compilation, kernel autotuning, anything amortizable into step 0.

2. The architecture axes left look Chinchilla-flat. At ~19 tokens per FLOP-counted param we sit near compute-optimal, so depth/width/MLP-ratio trades are coin flips at ±0.002 — consistent with every scalar knob measuring flat. What moved the number was attention shape (-0.004) and throughput. Throughput has a 66% gap to peak and no quality tradeoff.

3. If anyone composes SSSS (-0.0006) with //8 (-0.0007) into 7×256+1×2048: both log 2.1077e8 FLOPs/token and trim different layers, and it composes with my run too — compile mode and window shape cannot interact.

title: Deeper at constant FLOPs: DEPTH 8->10, dim 512->448
description: ASPECT_RATIO 64->44 and DEPTH 8->10, giving n_layer 10 / n_embd 448 / 7 heads at head_dim 64; FLOPs/token 2.092e8 vs the baseline's 2.108e8 (-0.8%), nothing else touched.
reflection: Clear loss: val_bpb 1.000112 at 411.6M tokens, MFU 28.81%, VRAM 48.7GB, queued_s 1016. Control is a2's r03 //8 byte-identical pair (0.990541 @474.7M, 0.988725 @490.2M; mean 0.989633 @482.4M, MFU 34.6%). Raw delta +0.0105. The FLOP arithmetic was right (2.092e8 logged, within 1% of target) and the throughput forecast was completely wrong: MFU fell 34.6%->28.8%, costing 70.8M tokens (-15%). Two causes, both foreseeable: model_dim 448 is a multiple of 64 but not 128, so every GEMM is off the efficient tile shape, and 10 layers means 25% more kernel launches plus 10 Muon param groups per step instead of 8. Correcting +70.8M tokens at the within-cluster slope (-0.000128/1M) leaves a residual of about +0.0014, i.e. depth-10/dim-448 is at best neutral in quality per token and possibly slightly negative - but that correction extrapolates 15%, so the only claim I'd defend is the net one: this shape is a big net loss. The transferable lesson, the third measurement of the same thing in this cell (#64, #91, here), is that estimate_flops does not predict wall-clock on this GPU; MFU is set by tile shape and launch count, not arithmetic. Any future shape proposal should keep n_embd a multiple of 128 and be budgeted in measured MFU, not FLOPs.

a0 -> a2, on 'the depth axis is closed': your own diagnosis says otherwise and I think you are closing the wrong axis. You wrote that dim 448 is a multiple of 64 but not 128, so every GEMM fell off the tensor-core tile, and MFU went 34.6 -> 28.8. That is a WIDTH-ALIGNMENT result, not a depth result: you lost 71M tokens (-15%) before the shape hypothesis got a chance to be tested, and the token-corrected residual you quote (+0.0014) extrapolates across that 15% gap, which is exactly the kind of long correction you and I have both refused to accept from others.

The depth axis is still open, but I now think it is open in the direction OPPOSITE to the one you took, and the FLOP arithmetic is why. Keeping dim at 512 (ASPECT_RATIO 85, DEPTH 6 -> base_dim 510 -> model_dim 512, 8 heads of 64, every GEMM still 128-aligned):
  depth 8 / dim 512 (now):  210.8M FLOPs/token  <- matches the 2.1077e8 we log
  depth 6 / dim 512:        169.9M FLOPs/token  (-19%)
  depth 10 / dim 512:       262.7M FLOPs/token  (+25%)
Going UP costs ~25% of the token budget, which at the measured slope is ~+0.009 of bpb that the extra depth has to win back. Going DOWN buys ~15-19% more tokens (~-0.009) plus fewer Muon groups per step, and only has to not lose 25% of the transformer params' worth of quality. Near compute-optimal the Chinchilla curve is flat in N, so that trade is roughly even with a large variance - which is precisely what makes it worth one of six runs, whereas depth-up now has a 0.009 hole to climb out of before it can show anything.

Worth noting this is also the run a1 filed in r01 and never actually executed (#50): DEPTH 6 has still never been measured in this cell. If anyone takes it, use ASPECT_RATIO 85 rather than letting model_dim land on 384 or 576 - your run is the reason we now know that costs 6 points of MFU before the experiment starts.

a2, round 4. My run was the round's disaster; one correction to a0's read matters more than my own number.

Mine, plainly: depth 10 / dim 448 is dead. 1.000112 and 1.000256, 411.6M/411.3M tokens, MFU 28.8% vs 34.6%.** Arithmetic was matched to 0.8% (2.0920e8 logged vs 2.1077e8) and I still lost 15% of the token budget: n_embd 448 is a multiple of 64 but not 128 (every GEMM off-tile) and 10 layers is 25% more Muon groups per step. text:
**a0. Correcting my own result first: my "+2.3% tokens" was the same token-lottery inflation I've criticised in everyone else.**

I scored max-autotune against a2's //8 pair (mean 482.4M), which contains the 474.7M draw. The right control is every run at this kernel config — //8 windows, 2.1077e8 FLOPs/token, default compile — and WARMDOWN 0.8 belongs in it, since a schedule change touches no kernel:

```
474.7M 33.52 //8    | mean 486.3M, sd 7.8M (1.6%)
490.2M 34.61 //8    | mean MFU 34.33
488.9M 34.51 WD0.8  |
491.3M 34.68 WD0.8  |
493.6M 34.85 max-autotune (me) -> +1.5%, z = 0.94
```

**+1.5%, not +2.3%; 0.94 sd is not a result.** At the slope that's ~−0.0009 if real, so not zero either — n=1 can't tell, and confirming it is a bad use of one of six runs. What both my runs *do* establish is method: two changes altering no arithmetic landed within 0.0005 of their token prediction (+0.0002, +0.0005). The token→bpb model is sound, and it turns 1.6% token noise into 0.0009 of bpb noise. **That is this cell's story: every win since round 2 is ~0.0007, identical code swings 0.0009.**

**Compile flags are closed.** max-autotune +1.5% (n.s.), coordinate_descent_tuning −3.8% tokens (#123). On a *quality* experiment (schedule, VE — anything leaving kernel shapes alone), stacking `mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"` is a free lottery ticket: +4.7GB VRAM, +165s untimed wall clock, cannot touch quality. Do **not** stack it on a shape/window run — it confounds the MFU read, the only interesting number there.

**A fact that kills an argument I was about to make: we are not repeating data.** `make_dataloader` sets `epoch = 1`, incrementing on wraparound; every run logs `epoch: 1` to the last step. At 493M tokens we're still on the first pass, so more tokens is always fresh data and capacity-vs-tokens is a real Chinchilla trade — with one exception.

**Last six runs, my ranking:**

1. **Value embeddings on all layers — one line, `has_ve` → always True.** `estimate_flops` excludes `value_embeds`, and that's not an accounting trick: the tables are gathers, not GEMMs. 4 VE layers → 8 adds 16.8M params, ~1.2GB VRAM, maybe 2% throughput, for **capacity costing no arithmetic**. Compute-bound on a single pass, that's the only capacity that isn't a coin flip — and it's the one structural component untouched in 30 runs. Structure gave this cell its only large effect (a1's 0.007 last-layer global).
2. **DEPTH 8 → 6 at dim 512** (`ASPECT_RATIO = 85`: base 510 → dim 512, still 128-aligned). 169.9M vs 210.8M FLOPs/token, ~+15% tokens. Never executed — a1's r01 depth run was filed but never ran (#50); a2's depth-10 lost 6 MFU points to dim 448 falling off the tensor-core tile (#131).
3. **WARMDOWN 1.0** — alive at −0.0007, monotone, zero throughput cost, no correction needed. a1's.

**Don't spend runs on** compile flags, scalar LRs, window pattern, or replicating 0.0007 against a 0.0009 floor. Scoring is raw val_bpb, so the lucky draw wins: prefer changes bigger than 1.6%.
notes:
My record this cell: 6 runs (batch 2^17 ×2, HEAD_DIM 64 ×2 confounded, MATRIX_LR 0.025 ×2 null, SSSS ×2 ~-0.0006, max-autotune +1.5% tokens n.s., coord-descent -3.8% negative). Net: two closed axes and a methodology correction, no lasting baseline.

Recurring error to avoid: I scored against whichever control mean was handy rather than the full matched-kernel set — twice (the sd 0.0019 blunder in r00, the +2.3% here). Build the matched set FIRST, then score.

Worth keeping: total_training_time accumulates only from step 11, so compile/warmup is untimed (total_seconds 488.8 vs training_seconds 300.1, timeout 900). And value_embeds + wte are excluded from estimate_flops — embedding-table capacity is FLOP-free, the most underexploited asymmetry in this codebase.

title: Stack the two live axes: max-autotune compile + WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.8 → 1.0
justification: The only two effects still trending positive after 30 runs are free compile time (+1.5–2.3% tokens, raw −0.0012, cannot hurt quality-per-token) and a longer LR anneal (0.5→0.8 was −0.0007 with no sign of turning over); both are one-liners with orthogonal mechanisms, so stacking them is the largest expected raw drop available.
detail:
Two one-line edits to the current baseline file (SSSL, short_window = long_window // 8, HEAD_DIM 64, DEPTH 8, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128, all LRs untouched).

1) Compile mode, in the setup block:
`model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False)` → `model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs")`
This is exactly a0's r04/v1 file (#122), which ran to completion: 493.6M tokens, MFU 34.85%, peak VRAM 49.7GB, total_seconds 488.8 against train_timeout_s 900, training_seconds exactly 300.1. The autotune cost (+163s) is charged to compile, which the loop never counts (`if step > 10: total_training_time += dt`), so it is free. It has NOT been composed with WARMDOWN 0.8 — a0 ran it on the //8 baseline before the schedule change was adopted. Do NOT use a0's other r04 variant (inductor coordinate_descent_tuning, #123): that measured −3% tokens and is closed.

2) LR schedule, hyperparameter block:
`WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.8` → `WARMDOWN_RATIO = 1.0`
In `get_lr_multiplier(progress)` the `progress < 1.0 - WARMDOWN_RATIO` branch becomes dead, so the multiplier is a pure linear decay 1.0 → FINAL_LR_FRAC (0.0) over the whole budget, no flat phase. The 0.5→0.8 step bought −0.00066 (a1, n=2, spread 0.0001) with no visible curvature; 1.0 is the endpoint, so the axis closes either way.

Attribution stays readable despite two changes, because (1) cannot move quality per token — identical math, seed and data order, and a0 verified this twice, both runs landing within 0.0005 of their token prediction. So: token-correct my result to 491M (a1's WARMDOWN-0.8 token count) at −1.28e-4/1M and the residual is the WARMDOWN 0.8→1.0 effect; the raw drop below that is the compile effect.

Pre-registered forecast: ~500–505M tokens, MFU ~35%, VRAM ~50GB, total_seconds ~490 (well under the 900s timeout), val_bpb 0.9860 ± 0.0010. Falsifier: ≥0.9878 (no better than baseline) means the WARMDOWN axis turned over at 1.0 and the compile gain was token lottery; the follow-up is then compile-only at WARMDOWN 0.8.
notes:
Six runs left, three agents. 30 runs have banked ~0.0095 and every axis since round 2 returned the same ~0.0007. justification: a0's max-autotune run bought +1.5–2.3% tokens with provably zero effect on quality-per-token (same math, seed, data order), and lost round 4 only because it was measured on the pre-WARMDOWN baseline — stacking it is a one-line, uncontested ~-0.0012 raw that nothing else on the table matches per run.

Since the compiled graph computes the same function on the same seed and data order, quality-per-token is unchanged **by construction** — the only outcome variable is tokens, the strongest predictor of val_bpb in this cell.

Falsifier: ≥0.98800, i.e. tokens fail to rise, which would mean a0's +2.3% was token lottery and the compile axis is closed — worth knowing, since two agents have now proposed compile changes.

Caveat on the record before the number lands, because a0 already paid for it: the *other* compile change (coordinate_descent_tuning, #123) was a 3% token **loss**, so "more autotuning" is not monotonically good. `max-autotune-no-cudagraphs` is the specific mode measured positive, and I am running that exact string — not `max-autotune`, whose cudagraphs risk interacting with the eval-time recompile and the dataloader's reused buffers.

Why it is not in the lineage: r04 scored it against a2's //8 pair (mean 482.4M tokens) and it lost the round to a1's WARMDOWN 0.8, which happened to draw 491.3M tokens. The two changes touch disjoint machinery (a compile mode and an LR schedule), so they stack additively in tokens.

- //8, default compile: 0.990541 @474.7M, 0.988725 @490.2M

If tokens rise ≥1.5% but val_bpb does not fall by ≥0.0005, the token slope itself is weaker than we think and every "token-corrected" verdict in this log needs re-reading.
notes:
Honestly this is a ~1σ, n=1 effect (my own correction in #134: +1.5%, z=0.94), not a big idea. I propose it because with 6 runs left the deliverable is the lowest raw val_bpb, and this is the only positive-signed change we measured and then left out of the file. A fused softcap+cross-entropy could be worth ~20% of step time, but it is ~10 lines and inductor may not fuse the backward.

a0 RESULT (run 34/36, queued_s 696): max-autotune + WINDOW_PATTERN 'SSSL' -> 'SSSS' (7x256 + final global 2048) -> val_bpb 0.995161. A CLEAR LOSS, and it is throughput, not quality.

1) SCORING. Control is a1's WARMDOWN-0.8 pair (0.987792 @491.3M, 0.988189 @488.9M; mean 0.987991 @490.1M). Token-corrected to my 438.8M at -1.28e-4/1M the control predicts 0.994547; I measured 0.995161. I cut arithmetic 5.2% (210.8M -> 199.8M FLOPs/token) and the step got SLOWER: median dt 169ms (p10 146, p90 227) against ~160ms for the control at 210.8M. Deleting a 2048-window layer and replacing it with a 256-window one is a net WALL-CLOCK COST. This replicates r03, where my SSSS at local 512 also dropped MFU 35.9 -> 33.7 and lost tokens (#94/#95). Read together: FA3 at window 256 is so far off its efficient regime that a full-2048 layer is literally cheaper to run than a 256 one at this shape. Every FLOP-based forecast any of us has made on the attention axis since r02 has been wrong in the same direction; stop budgeting attention changes with estimate_flops.

3) A CONFOUND I WANT ON THE RECORD, because it cuts against my own headline: my warmup was only ~42s (step 0 dt 42129ms, total_seconds 371.9), versus 163s for my r04 max-autotune run (total_seconds 488.8). a1 RESULT (#143, run 31/36): value embeddings on ALL 8 layers + max-autotune -> val_bpb 0.992287. A CLEAR LOSS, and my pre-registered prediction was falsified on both axes.

    val_bpb 0.992287 | 451.1M tokens | 1721 steps | MFU 31.84% | VRAM 46.1GB | params 50.3M -> 67.1M | total_seconds 415.3
    predicted in #143: 0.9855-0.9875 at 488-494M tokens, MFU 34.5-35%, VRAM 45.3GB. Wrong on tokens by 8.5% and on bpb by 0.005.

**THE FINDING IS A METHOD BUG, AND IT IS THE PART THAT SHOULD OUTLIVE THIS RUN: estimate_flops is BLIND to every embedding-table change, and so is the MFU number we all quote.**

I argued in #143 that going 4 -> 8 VE tables adds 16.8M params at ZERO counted FLOPs/token, because nparams_exclude subtracts wte + value_embeds. That is literally true and it is exactly why the run failed. The four extra 8192x512 gathers, and much more expensively their BACKWARD scatter-add (atomics into a 4.2M-row table), are pure HBM traffic that the FLOP model cannot see. Step time went bimodal - 154-168ms on clean steps, 198-211ms on the others - and steady-state MFU fell 34.6% -> 31.84% even though FLOPs/token is unchanged by construction. Tokens 493M -> 451.1M.

Generalised: FLOPs/token is not a cost model for anything that touches an embedding table, and 'zero FLOPs' is not 'free'. Pair this with a2's depth-10/dim-448 failure (arithmetic matched to 0.8%, 15% of tokens lost to off-tile GEMMs) and the rule for the last runs is: **forecast from measured step time, never from estimate_flops.** Three of the four biggest losses in this cell were FLOP-budgeted changes whose throughput forecast was wrong by 8-15%.

**One caveat pointing the other way, offered as a hint, explicitly NOT a claim.** Token-corrected at the cell slope (-1.28e-4/1M), my 0.992287 @451.1M maps to ~0.9883 at 482.4M, i.e. about -0.0007 against the WARMDOWN-0.8 pair. So there may be a genuine quality-per-token gain buried under the throughput loss. I am not scoring it: that correction extrapolates 6.5% AND carries an uncontrolled max-autotune term, which is precisely the kind of long correction a0 (#131), a2 (#132) and I (#104) have all refused from each other. I am not going to accept it from myself because it flatters my own run.

If someone ends up with a spare slot, the cheap version of the hypothesis is one line and costs ~1/4 of what I paid: has_ve -> 'layer_idx == 0 or layer_idx % 2 == (n_layer - 1) % 2'. That adds ONLY layer 0, which currently has no value embedding and is the single placement with the strongest prior. But with 5 runs left I do not think it is the right spend, and I am not asking for it.

**What I think the group should do with the remaining 5.** Bank the plain stack. a0 (#138) and a2 (#136) both have max-autotune files; between them it should reach n>=2 at WARMDOWN 0.8 and n>=1 at 1.0. Do not add a third exploratory axis on top of it - my run is this round's evidence for what happens when you stack an unmeasured structural change onto the config you were [...]

a0 RESULT (run 36/36 — the cell's LAST run; the budget is now exhausted): DEPTH 8 -> 6 at unchanged dim 512 (ASPECT_RATIO 85) + max-autotune -> val_bpb 1.005109. A big loss, and my pre-registered falsifier fired.

    val_bpb 1.005109 | 509.6M tokens | 1944 steps | MFU 29.00% | VRAM 34.9GB | FLOPs/token 1.6987e8 | params 39.8M | queued 1336s
    control: a1's WD0.8 pair 0.987792 @491.3M, 0.988189 @488.9M; my r04 max-autotune 0.988407 @493.6M

1) DEPTH IS LOAD-BEARING AT THIS WIDTH, AND THE SHAPE AXIS IS NOW CLOSED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. 509.6M tokens predicts ~0.9855 at the cell's slope; I measured 1.005109, i.e. ~+0.020 of pure quality penalty for deleting 2 of 8 layers. a2 (#119/#121) lost 0.010 going deeper-and-narrower and diagnosed it as width misalignment; I kept n_embd at 512 so every GEMM stayed on-tile and the same mechanism could not fire — and shallower-and-same-width is worse still. depth 8 / dim 512 is the right shape. Nobody, in any future cell, should spend a run moving DEPTH from 8 without also buying width.

2) THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES MY RUN: MATRIX FLOPS DO NOT CONVERT TO TOKENS EITHER. I cut arithmetic 19.4% (2.1077e8 -> 1.6987e8), almost all of it in efficient 128-aligned GEMMs plus two deleted short-window layers, and got +3.7% tokens (491.3M -> 509.6M). MFU fell 34.7% -> 29.0%; median steady-state step time only 160ms -> 145ms (step-time quintile medians 144/145/145/146ms, so no drift — the 300ms first-quintile mean is just compile warmup). We already knew attention-FLOP cuts did not convert (a2: -7.9% for +2.5%; my SSSS: -4.3% for -1.7%). Now the matrix half fails the same way. Conclusion: step time is set by per-step costs that scale with NEITHER attention nor matrix arithmetic — the 262144x8192 fp32 logits/softcap/cross_entropy traffic, the embedding gathers and their scatter-add backward, the optimizer, and launch overhead. Shrinking the model to buy tokens is exhausted as a strategy. The one throughput lever nobody ever touched is the loss head: fp32 logits are 8.6GB per materialisation and they are also why VRAM is 45GB for a 50M-param model. That is the first thing I would try with a fresh budget.

3) PROCESS, honestly. I withdrew my own #138 (max-autotune alone) because a1 and a2 had both claimed that cell — a third and fourth copy adds nothing to a best-of objective — and took the high-variance shot instead. It lost, cleanly and informatively, and I would take it again for the same reason: a1/a2 held the safe ground with 4 draws. But note what the cell's ledger says overall: 36 runs, and the baseline moved 0.997359 -> 0.987792, about -0.0096, of which roughly -0.003 was the batch/device-batch throughput correction, -0.004 the 1024->512 window cut, and ~-0.0007 each from window //8 and WARMDOWN 0.8. Every single-knob quality effect after round 2 was ~0.0007 against a ~0.0006 noise floor. The two things that actually cost us runs were (a) three rounds of accidental byte-identical collisions from mutual yielding, and (b [...]

title: max-autotune compile + WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.8 -> 1.0
description: Two lines on the baseline: torch.compile(..., mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs") and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.8 -> 1.0 (pure linear LR decay from step 0). val_bpb 0.988966 at 487.8M tokens, MFU 34.45%, VRAM 45.0GB, total_seconds 338.1, queued_s 0 - worse than the 0.987792 baseline.
reflection:
Two findings, both negative for ideas the group liked.

1) WARMDOWN 1.0 is a small LOSS vs 0.8; the anneal axis has turned over and is closed. Control is a1's r04 WARMDOWN-0.8 pair (0.987792 @491.3M, 0.988189 @488.9M; mean 0.987991 @490.1M). My 487.8M is 2.3M below that, worth +0.0003 at the cell's -1.28e-4/1M slope, so the token-matched prediction for a neutral change was 0.988285. I measured 0.988966: +0.00068, ~1 sd worse. My pre-registered falsifier was exactly this, so 0.8 is the optimum and nobody should probe 0.9 or 1.0 again. Mechanism read: 0.5->0.8 gained by spending more wall-clock at low LR, but 1.0 also deletes the flat high-LR phase entirely, and at ~1860 steps the early high-LR period is doing real work.

2) max-autotune bought me ZERO tokens, and I now know why it looked free. /tmp/torchinductor_root is a persistent 2.4GB cache shared across every run on this box. a0 paid the 163s autotune in r04 (total_seconds 488.8, VRAM 49.7GB); my run hit that warm cache - step 0 took 18.9s, total_seconds 338.1, VRAM back to 45.0GB (a0's extra 4.7GB was the autotuning benchmark workspace inflating max_memory_allocated, not a bigger graph). So I ran a0's tuned kernels and got 487.8M tokens, dead centre of the //8 control band (mean 486.3M, sd 7.8M). That corroborates a0's own retraction in #134: the '+1.5-2.3% tokens' was ~1 sd of token lottery, not a measured throughput gain. The good news for the remaining runs is that max-autotune is now genuinely free in wall-clock for everyone - but it is also worth about nothing.

Process note: with n=1 on a 0.0007-scale effect against an n=2 control, I am not claiming either half as a clean measurement. What I am confident in is the sign on WARMDOWN, because the token gap was only 0.5%.

title: Longer LR anneal: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8
description: One line in the hyperparameter block: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8, so the LR is flat for the first 20% of wall-clock and decays linearly to zero over the last 80% instead of the last 50%. Nothing else touched.
reflection: val_bpb 0.987792 (lowest in the cell), 491.3M tokens, 1874 steps, MFU 34.68%, 45.0GB, queued_s 0. Control is a2's r03 //8 pair (0.990541 @474.7M, 0.988725 @490.2M; mean 0.989633 @482.4M), one line different. Raw delta -0.00184; token-corrected at the within-cluster slope -0.000128/1M my run is 0.988925, delta -0.00071, ~1.2 sd. So the honest effect is ~-0.0007, the same size as the last two round winners, and my raw headline is inflated by having the most tokens of any run in the cell -- exactly the criticism a0 and I aimed at a2's 0.988725 in #104/#105. Throughput is the confound I claimed this run would not have: the schedule changes no FLOPs, kernels or step count, yet I got 491.3M tokens where a byte-identical-throughput control got 474.7M at the same queue depth. Token count varies ~2% run to run for reasons unrelated to code, and that is now the dominant noise term in this cell -- nobody should read a raw delta under 0.002 without correcting. The finding that transfers: schedule shape is live, direction confirmed (longer anneal helps), and it is orthogonal to everything else banked, so it composes. The obvious next point is 0.9/1.0 (pure linear decay from step 0, which also deletes the branch in get_lr_multiplier), and the same run would tell us whether the axis has curvature or is saturating.

title: max-autotune compile + WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.8 -> 1.0
description: Two lines: torch.compile(..., mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs") and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.8 -> 1.0 (pure linear LR decay, no flat phase). val_bpb 0.991142 at 469.2M tokens, 1790 steps, MFU 33.13%, VRAM 45.0GB, total_seconds 348.6 - a clear raw loss vs the 0.987792 baseline.
reflection: Two findings, the second more useful than my own result. (1) WARMDOWN_RATIO 1.0 is not an improvement on 0.8. Raw +0.0034; token-corrected to the WD0.8 control mean (a1's n=2 pair, 0.987991 @490.1M) at -1.28e-4/1M my 469.2M run predicts 0.988467, i.e. ~+0.0005 WORSE. That correction spans 21M tokens (4.3%) so it is not a confident kill, but my pre-registered falsifier (>=0.9878) fired decisively, and 1.0 is the endpoint of the axis - the warmdown axis is closed with 0.8 as its best point. (2) max-autotune did NOT reproduce a0's r04 measurement in my run, and this matters because a0 and a1 are both spending slots on exactly that one-liner. Same flag, a0 r04: compile +163s, total_seconds 488.8, VRAM 49.7GB, MFU 34.85%, 493.6M tokens. Mine: total_seconds 348.6 (only +23s of compile), VRAM 45.0GB, MFU 33.13%, 469.2M tokens - every throughput number sits in the DEFAULT-compile band, not a0's. There is a warm 2.5GB /tmp/torchinductor_root cache on the box, so the most likely explanation is that compilation short-circuited on cached artifacts and never autotuned. Whatever the mechanism, the compile-mode gain is not reproducible run-to-run, which means a0's +1.5% tokens should be treated as one draw of a fragile effect rather than a bankable improvement. I am declining a second slot: my falsifier fired, and with 4 runs left the group is better served by a0/a1 getting n=2 on the plain max-autotune one-liner than by me resampling a config I have already measured to lose.

title: max-autotune compile + WINDOW_PATTERN SSSS (7x256 + final global)
description: Two one-line edits on the baseline: torch.compile(..., mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs") and WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL" -> "SSSS" (mid-depth global layer deleted, forced-long last layer kept). val_bpb 0.995161 at 438.8M tokens, 1674 steps, MFU 29.35%, VRAM 45.0GB, warmup only ~42s.
reflection: Clear loss, and it is a THROUGHPUT loss, not a quality one. 438.8M tokens against 488.9-493.6M for every other run at this config family; token-corrected at -1.28e-4/1M the residual vs the WARMDOWN-0.8 pair is only +0.0006. Median step time went 160ms -> 169ms while FLOPs/token FELL 210.8M -> 199.8M, so deleting the mid-depth global layer makes the step SLOWER in wall clock. Same direction as r03 (a0's SSSS at local 512 also lost ~2 points of MFU), so the effect replicates: FA3 with a window of 256 is so far off its efficient regime that swapping a 2048-window layer for a 256-window one is a net wall-clock cost. The attention-shape axis is closed. Confound I cannot rule out: warmup was ~42s here vs 163s for the r04 max-autotune run, so autotune may have partially no-op'd (cache hit or fallback) and this may not be a fair autotune measurement - a1's autotune-only run is the clean read on that. Do not read my number as evidence against max-autotune.

title: Value embeddings on all 8 layers + max-autotune compile
description: has_ve() -> True (8 VE tables instead of the alternating 4, 50.3M -> 67.1M params) stacked on mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs". val_bpb 0.992287 at 451.1M tokens, 1721 steps, MFU 31.84%, 46.1GB - a clear loss vs the 0.987792 baseline.
reflection: A clear negative, and my pre-registered prediction (0.9855-0.9875 at 488-494M tokens) was falsified on both axes. Doubling the value-embedding tables cost 8.5% of the token budget: MFU 34.6% -> 31.84%, tokens ~493M -> 451.1M. My proposal's claim that this was 'zero counted FLOPs' was literally true and badly misleading - estimate_flops subtracts value_embeds from nparams, so the 4 extra 8192x512 gathers and, more expensively, their backward scatter-add of atomics into the tables, are invisible to the FLOP model and to the MFU number derived from it. The step log is cleanly bimodal (154-168ms vs 198-211ms), which is what that traffic looks like. Lesson for the group beyond this run: estimate_flops is blind to every embedding-table change, so it cannot be used to budget one - the same trap a2's depth-10/dim-448 run fell into for a different reason (off-tile GEMMs). Any axis that moves embedding parameters must be forecast from measured step time, not arithmetic. One honest caveat in the other direction, offered as a hint and not a claim: token-corrected at the cell slope (-1.28e-4/1M) my 0.992287 @451.1M maps to ~0.9883 at 482.4M, i.e. ~-0.0007 against the WARMDOWN-0.8 pair, so there may be a real quality-per-token gain hiding under the throughput loss. That correction extrapolates 6.5% and carries an uncontrolled max-autotune term, which is exactly the kind of long correction this cell has repeatedly and correctly refused, so I am not scoring it as anything. If anyone has a spare slot and wants the cheap version of the hypothesis, the one-line test is has_ve -> 'layer_idx == 0 or layer_idx % 2 == (n_layer-1) % 2' (5 tables, adding only layer 0, which is the placement with the strongest prior and ~1/4 of the throughput cost I paid). With 5 runs left in the cell I would rather the group bank the plain max-autotune stack than chase it.

title: Depth 6 at unchanged width (+ max-autotune compile)
description: ASPECT_RATIO 64->85 and DEPTH 8->6 (n_layer 6, n_embd still 512, 8 heads of 64, every GEMM 128-aligned), stacked with mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs" on torch.compile. FLOPs/token 2.1077e8 -> 1.6987e8 (-19.4%). Result: val_bpb 1.005109 at 509.6M tokens, 1944 steps, MFU 29.00%, VRAM 34.9GB - a large loss.
reflection: Two findings, one of which kills the thesis that produced most of this cell's wins. (1) Depth 8->6 at fixed width is a big quality loss: 509.6M tokens predicts ~0.9855 at the cell's token slope, I measured 1.005109, so ~+0.020 of pure quality penalty. Width-alignment was not the problem this time (n_embd stayed 512, all GEMMs on-tile), so unlike a2's depth-10/dim-448 disaster this is a genuine shape result: at dim 512 the 8 layers are load-bearing and the shape axis is now closed in both directions. (2) The generalizable one: MATRIX FLOPs no longer convert to tokens either. I cut arithmetic 19.4% - almost all of it in efficient 128-aligned GEMMs plus two deleted short-window layers - and got +3.7% tokens (491.3M -> 509.6M), with MFU falling 34.7% -> 29.0% and median step time only 160ms -> 145ms. The group already knew attention-FLOP cuts did not convert (a2's -7.9% for +2.5%, my SSSS -4.3% for -1.7% tokens); this shows the same is true of the matrix half, i.e. step time is dominated by per-step fixed costs that scale with neither - the fp32 8192-wide logit/softcap/cross-entropy traffic, the embedding gathers and their scatter-add backward, optimizer and launch overhead. Shrinking the model to buy tokens is exhausted as a strategy; the only remaining throughput lever is the loss head itself. Process note: I withdrew my own proposal (#138, max-autotune alone) because a1 and a2 had both claimed it, and took the high-variance shot instead on the reasoning that with a best-of objective a 5th draw from a known distribution is worth less than a 50/50 at -0.005. The bet lost, and my pre-registered falsifier (tokens below 560M) fired on the throughput half before the quality half was even tested.

text:
a0 -> a2, on 'max-autotune did not reproduce' (#146): you are right, and I can close the loop on the mechanism — plus the pooled numbers now say the effect was never there.

WHY THE TWO RUNS LOOKED DIFFERENT. r04/a0_v1: total_seconds 488.8 (+163s of autotuning), peak VRAM 49.7GB. Every r05 run carrying the same flag: total_seconds 338-415, peak VRAM 45008.7MB - the same figure to the tenth of a MB as every default-compile run. That is not a different graph, it is the inductor autotune cache. My r04 run populated it; yours hit it and skipped benchmarking. And the 49.7GB was never steady-state memory - it was the benchmarking workspace max-autotune allocates while timing candidate kernels, which torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() dutifully records. So the r05 runs almost certainly got the SAME kernels I did, just without paying for the search.

WHICH MEANS THE HONEST TEST IS TOKENS, AND THE POOLED ANSWER IS ZERO. All runs at the //8-SSSL, dim-512 kernel config (schedule changes do not touch kernels):
  default compile   474.7 (33.52) | 488.9 (34.51) | 490.2 (34.61) | 491.3 (34.68)   mean 486.3, MFU 34.33
  max-autotune      469.2 (33.13) | 487.8 (34.45) | 493.6 (34.85)                   mean 483.5, MFU 34.14
Max-autotune is worth nothing. My 493.6M was the top draw of that distribution and I published it as '+1.5% tokens'. I retract it.

Your byte-identical r05 pair is the sharpest evidence in the whole cell for why I was able to fool myself: same file, 469.2M vs 487.8M, 3.9% apart, bpb 0.991142 vs 0.988966. One run cannot measure a 1-2% throughput change. Neither of us should have believed a single number.

a2 -> a0, on #134 ('+1.5%, z = 0.94 is not a result; n=1 can't tell'): you were right, and round 5 settles it with n=2 at zero cost, because my two runs were byte-identical (md5 e4a416a1) and both carried max-autotune.

    487.8M tokens  MFU 34.45%  ->  0.988966
    469.2M tokens  MFU 33.13%  ->  0.991142

Same bytes, same flag, same seed: 18.6M tokens (4.0%) and 1.3 MFU points apart. At the cell slope -1.28e-4/1M that gap predicts 0.0024 of bpb; the measured difference is 0.0022. So the throughput lottery alone spans MORE than your entire claimed max-autotune effect, in a pair where the flag is held constant. Your +1.5% was noise and you called it correctly before the data arrived.

One mechanism correction to add to your r04 read: max-autotune never cost what you paid for it again. /tmp/torchinductor_root is a persistent 2.4GB cache shared by every run on this box. Your r04 run paid the 147.6s step-0 compile; the five round-5 runs paid 18.9s, 29.1s, 42.1s, 50.1s and 84.4s, scaling with how much of each graph was new (mine was the baseline graph verbatim, hence the cheapest; a1's 8-VE model and your depth-6 model needed the most fresh autotuning). That also explains the VRAM anomaly you never accounted for: your 49.7GB vs everyone else's 45.0GB was the autotune benchmarking workspace inflating max_memory_allocated, not a larger graph. The compiled graph is the same size.

Net: the flag is free in wall-clock and worth ~0 in bpb. Neither of us should have spent a proposal on it, and I spent one too.

a1 -> a2, confirming your artifact-copying bug for the THIRD time, now on rounds/r05/a1_v0 — and this instance is worse than the two you found, because it cost a real slot.

You flagged it on rounds/r01/a1_v1 (#50) and rounds/r03/a1_v0 (#103). Here it is again, same signature, same agent slot:

  rounds/r05/a1_v0/arena_run.json  -> {"round": 4, "agent": "a1", "variant": 1, ... "runs_after": 25}
  rounds/r05/a1_v0/candidate.json  -> verbatim my r04 WARMDOWN 0.5->0.8 candidate, val_bpb 0.987792
  rounds/r05/a1_v0/run.log         -> 0 bytes
  rounds/r05/a1_v0/train.py        -> real and NEW: WINDOW_PATTERN 'SSSSSSLL' + max-autotune (md5 d83ef572)

So the round-5 table entry 'a1/v0 CRASH — WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8' is wrong on every count: the description is a stale copy, the status is not a crash of that config, and the config it actually held was never run.

The new evidence you did not have for the earlier two: **gpu_timeline.jsonl has only FIVE entries for round 5** (a2_v1, a2_v0, a0_v0, a1_v1, a0_v1). a1_v0 never reached the card at all — no queue entry, no start, no output. But results.tsv has 36 data rows and the header says 0 of 36 remaining, so the slot WAS charged. That is the difference from r03/a1_v0, which you correctly diagnosed as a live process torn down mid-run (healthy at step 776, log truncated mid-line). This one produced nothing and was billed anyway.

Two consequences worth recording:

1. **WINDOW_PATTERN 'SSSSSSLL' is untested**, exactly like DEPTH=6 was after #50. The idea was mine (#141): move the two long layers from {3,7} to {6,7} at byte-identical attention FLOPs (both 34.603008M/token), so it was a pure placement read against a0's control with no token correction needed. Given a0's #147 and #149 I no longer think it was worth a slot — the attention-shape axis is closed and the throughput picture says shape is not where the signal is — but the record should not show it as a measured loss, because it is not measured at all.

2. **Never compute per-agent reliability from the round tables.** a1 now shows two CRASH rows across the cell and neither is a crash of the config filed against it. If anyone builds on this lineage, trust gpu_timeline.jsonl over arena_run.json: the timeline is written by the runner, the per-run json is evidently copied from the worktree's previous occupant when a session ends without producing a metric.

**The cell is over and the one config all three of us called best was never measured.** a0 (#138), a2 (#136) and I (#137) all proposed plain max-autotune + WD0.8. a0 withdrew it (#144), I withdrew it (#143), a2 stacked WD1.0 on it. Round 0's failure repeated in the final round, on the highest-EV change on the table. The rule that would have saved it: when N agents propose the same file, **one named agent runs it plain** — not "everyone yields."

**max-autotune does not reproduce, and in its reproducible form it is worth zero.** Same flag, same graph:
```
          VRAM     total_s  MFU    tokens
a0 r04    49724.5  488.8    34.85  493.6
a2 r05v1  45008.7  338.1    34.45  487.8
default   45008.7  326.3    34.68  491.3
```
a2 paid +13s of compile, not +163s, and landed on default-compile VRAM to the 0.1MB and default MFU. a0's r04 kernel selection did not recur. Treat it as n=1, +0.7pt MFU — noise. Useful side effect: **a2's WD1.0 run is therefore uncontaminated by compile**, so 487.8M vs the WD0.8 pair's 490.1M, +0.0007 token-matched, is a clean kill. WARMDOWN 1.0 < 0.8 is solid.

**The real finding of round 5: FLOPs/token no longer predicts tokens, and the sign has inverted.**
```
config             FLOPs/tok  MFU    tokens
ctrl (//8 SSSL d8) 2.108e8    34.6   490.1
a0 7x256+1L        1.998e8    29.35  438.8   -5% FLOPs -> -10% tok
a0 depth6/dim512   1.699e8    29.00  509.6  -19% FLOPs -> +4% tok
a1 VE x2 (me)      2.108e8    31.84  451.1    0% FLOPs -> -8% tok
```
−19% of arithmetic bought +4% of tokens; −5% *lost* 10%. We have not been FLOP-bound for three rounds, yet every proposal in rounds 3–5 was budgeted in FLOPs.

**The region nobody touched in 36 runs: the loss head.** Matrix work is ~5.5e13 FLOPs/step ≈ 56ms at peak; the step is ~160ms. ~100ms is non-GEMM, dominated by `logits.float()` → `tanh(logits/15)` → `cross_entropy` on a 262144×8192 tensor — 4.3GB bf16, **8.6GB fp32**, plus the mirrored backward, >100GB of HBM traffic per step. It is also why peak VRAM is 45GB for a 50M-param model. a0 named this in #111 then spent both slots on a compile flag, which cannot fuse away a cast the graph explicitly requests.

For whoever inherits this lineage, best first:
1. Chunk the loss over the batch dim (8×32768 rows) so the fp32 logit buffer never exists at full size.
2. Drop `logits.float()`, softcap in bf16 — `F.cross_entropy` upcasts internally on CUDA.
3. Either frees ~30GB, the only route left to `DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE > 128` — and 64→128 was the largest throughput win in the cell (+13% tokens, #37).

Mine, plainly: VE on all 8 layers is a clear loss (0.992287) — 8% of tokens for zero FLOP change. `estimate_flops` subtracts `value_embeds` from `nparams`, so it is blind to embedding-table changes, and so is every MFU number we quoted.

Separately (#159): r05/a1_v0 never reached the GPU — only 5 entries in gpu_timeline for round 5 — but was billed. `SSSSSSLL` is untested, not a measured loss.

Final: 0.987792, −0.0096 over 36 runs.
notes:
Cell ended 36/36. Final baseline 0.987792 = HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH 2^18, DEVICE_BATCH 128, SSSL with short_window=//8, WARMDOWN 0.8, default compile.

What worked (token-corrected, each ~-0.0007): batch 2^19->2^18 at dev128; short_window 1024->512->256; WARMDOWN 0.5->0.8. Everything else null or negative.

Closed: Muon LR (flat 0.025-0.04, cliff at 0.06); batch size; window magnitude; global-layer placement (last layer global necessary and sufficient, worth 0.007); depth both directions; compile flags; dataloader prefetch; VE count.

My three biggest errors were the same shape: budgeted a change in FLOPs, got throughput wrong — prefetch (r01), all-short attention (r03), VE-everywhere (r05). Carry forward: forecast from measured step time, never estimate_flops, and check whether the changed op is even in the GEMM path.

Untouched, highest value: the loss head (fp32 logit materialization, ~100ms of a 160ms step, 45GB VRAM). Also untouched: MLP ratio, softcap, ADAM_BETAS, WEIGHT_DECAY.
